summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She presented with elevated liver enzymes and moderate ascites on ultrasound. Her white blood cell count rose to 17,700, prompting a workup that included a diagnostic paracentesis. Ascitic fluid analysis showed a white blood cell count of 132 with 5% polymorphonuclear cells, consistent with portal hypertension, and a positive culture for Bacillus species deemed a contaminant. CT imaging revealed cardiomegaly and mild pulmonary edema suggestive of diastolic heart failure, along with an indeterminate left adnexal density. She experienced recurrent hypoglycemia likely due to insulin stacking from recent shortened dialysis sessions. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, insulin regimen adjustment, and in-hospital hemodialysis. She was discharged home with stable condition, new insulin dosing, and follow-up plans including liver MRI and pelvic ultrasound.
